Job Title: Transmission Line Design Engineer or Engineer-in-Training 
 Job Level: ENG B/C/D ( We welcome applications from individuals with all levels of experience and will adjust the title and role accordingly) 
 Date Posted: July 13, 2026
 Closing Date: open until the position is filled
 Job Type: Full-time Permanent
 Category: Internal/External Opportunities 
 Location: Calgary
 Powering a bright future starts with you! 
 At AltaLink, people are at the heart of our success. We are a team committed to doing the right thing for each other and our customers. We foster an environment that is inclusive, collaborative and high performing and we value personal accountability. Our people are empowered to continuously improve, deliver outstanding customer service and make a meaningful impact every day. We embrace the unique identities, experiences and perspectives of our workforce, reflecting the communities where we operate. Everyone at AltaLink can expect to work in a safe, respectful environment where trust and commitment are at the core of how we operate. 
 Oh, and, what do we do? 
 We power Alberta! Our transmission lines deliver electricity to millions of Albertans 24 hours a day, seven days a week. When you’re on our team, you’re supporting Alberta’s homes, farms, businesses and industries by providing the safe, reliable and affordable electricity they rely on. Whether working in the field or in the office, every AltaLinker contributes to keeping the lights on. Want to join our team? We’re excited to share that we are hiring a Transmission Line Design Engineer.   
 Job Description: 
 An exciting opportunity currently exists for a “Transmission Line Design Engineer” within the Project Development – Lines & Civil Engineering Department at AltaLink. Reporting to the Manager, Lines & Civil Engineering.
 The successful candidate will be responsible for the design, engineering, project development and technical delivery of high voltage transmission line facilities across AltaLink’s transmission line network, from early scoping and conceptual development through detailed design, construction support, close-out and final acceptance. The individual will work closely with internal and external stakeholders to ensure line modifications, line rebuilds, customer interconnections, greenfield transmission line projects and urgent restoration work are designed and supported with a high level of quality, safety, constructability and customer service. 
 The position requires experience in project scoping, design, implementation, technical decision-making, construction support and final acceptance. The role also requires the ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder design inputs, manage design changes, support external EPC and contractor resources, and provide clear technical direction under tight project or field response timelines. As a senior designer on the team, the individual will provide guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and designers. This includes supporting technical development, coaching, design review, and knowledge transfer for emerging engineers and EITs. This position will appeal to individuals looking to apply extensive transmission line design experience and leadership talents in a dynamic utility environment.
 Responsibilities: 
 Prepare detailed calculations, studies, bills of material and design packages for transmission line capital, customer, Direct Assign and system projects.
 Prepare PLS-CADD models for design package development and existing line clearance evaluations.
 Complete line design packages for all AltaLink transmission voltage classes, including 69kV, 138kV, 240kV and 500kV assets, including rebuilds, modifications, greenfield lines, customer interconnections and emergency restoration work.
 Lead preliminary line design, route and structure option development, constructability review, material selection and design change resolution for complex transmission projects.
 Apply base geotechnical knowledge when developing line designs, including understanding soil classifications, borehole/geotechnical investigation outputs, groundwater/bedrock considerations, soil strength/deformation behaviour, frost depth, corrosivity data and backfill requirements as they relate to transmission line foundation selection and constructability.
 Support transmission line foundation design decisions for direct-embed poles, drilled shafts/caissons, screw/helical/bucket piles, driven piles, micro-piles, grillage and pad/footing applications, including review of compression, uplift, shear and moment reactions.
 Coordinate with geotechnical consultants, civil/foundation designers, project managers, construction resources and pile/foundation contractors to define geotechnical scope, review investigation results and resolve foundation design or installation risks.
 Consider foundation risk mitigation during design and construction support, including cave-in/sloughing risk, high groundwater, shallow bedrock, gravel/boulder interference, casing/culvert needs, washed gravel/backfill selection and impacts to schedule, cost, safety and reliability.
 Provide timely and effective technical input to support the Project Development and Execution teams.
 Develop scope descriptions for project estimating and provide clear implementation direction to internal designers, external engineering consultants, EPC contractors, construction resources and field crews.
 Review and/or approve technical drawings and specifications submitted by internal designers or contractors to ensure each project meets acceptable standards for operability, functionality, maintainability, reliability, durability and safety.
 Support construction execution and project close-out by resolving field questions, material issues, redline updates, design clarifications and as-built/return-data requirements.
 Support engineering standards development, design practice improvements and application of current or historical code requirements, including AEUC, CSA and applicable ISO reliability requirements.
 Provide subject matter support for line optimization, line rating, thermal rating, reconductoring assessments, facility applications, information requests and regulatory/hearing support as required.
 Contribute to material governance, supplier engagement, technical specifications, procurement support and emergency spare/material strategy for transmission line assets.
 Build and maintain effective working relationships with suppliers, external technical engineering resources, construction resources, customers and other stakeholders that results in growing understanding, good decisions and effective cooperation.
 Report on project engineering status to Project Managers and the Engineering Manager.
 Mentor junior engineers, EITs and designers through technical coaching, design reviews, knowledge sharing and support toward professional development.
 Provide leadership support within the team as required, including coordination of team deliverables, technical prioritization and coverage for management or project leadership needs.
 Maintain competency with current industry standards and regulatory groups such as AEUC, CSA and ISO Rules.
 Demonstrate key behaviors and meet identified expectations outlined in our four cultural pillars – one team, continuous improvement, customer focus and personal accountability.
 Qualifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Civil or Electrical Engineering.
 EIT or Professional Engineer with the Association of Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) or qualifies for registration with APEGA.
 Transmission Line Design experience is considered an asset. 
 Proven ability to perform the responsibilities listed above. 
 Demonstrated experience delivering complex transmission line designs from concept through close-out, including coordination with project managers, external designers, contractors, suppliers and field stakeholders.
 Knowledge of standards and codes that apply to transmission line design and the ability to research and apply past code requirements to existing facilities in current situations, including Alberta power system facilities, Alberta Utility Code (AUC/AEUC) and Canadian Standards Association (CSA) requirements.
 Working knowledge of transmission line materials, structure families, insulator and hardware selection, conductor/OPGW applications, foundations, steel poles, wood poles and constructability considerations.
 Base knowledge of geotechnical investigation programs and geotechnical data used for transmission line design, including borehole/CPT information, soil classifications, soil strength and deformation behaviour, groundwater, bedrock, frost depth, corrosivity and backfill suitability.
 Base knowledge of transmission line foundation design and foundation reaction types, including compression, uplift, shear, overturning moment, lateral soil bearing, embedment depth, pile length/diameter considerations and pole/foundation deflection impacts.
 Ability to interpret geotechnical reports at a level sufficient to coordinate with geotechnical and civil/foundation specialists, identify design or constructability risks, and incorporate appropriate assumptions into line design packages.
 Experience in PLS-CADD and PLS-POLE is required.
 Experience using PLS-Tower, PLS-CAISSON, line rating tools, thermal rating methods, reconductoring assessments or line optimization studies would be an asset.
 Experience supporting customer interconnection, Direct Assign, Facility Application, AESO information request, regulatory/hearing or technical justification work would be an asset.
 Experience developing or applying engineering standards, technical specifications, material procurement requirements or supplier technical evaluations would be an asset.
 Experience with foundation-related standards, geotechnical scope development, foundation constructability reviews, or coordination of engineered foundation designs would be an asset.
 Superior organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage a wide variety of projects/issues simultaneously.
 Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work in a team environment with both office and field staff.
 Demonstrated ability to work under tight timelines and in high stress situations.
 Demonstrated mentoring, coaching or technical leadership experience with junior engineers, EITs, designers or cross-functional project teams.
 Must have a valid class 5 driver’s license.
 Ability and willingness to travel to site as required.
 Effective communication and interpersonal skills to interface with team members and customers to promote positive customer outcomes.
 Proven track record of good performance and attendance.

About us:  
 At Tall Tree, you’ll join an award-winning clinic focused on exceptional integrated healthcare. We’re a diverse team that is endlessly nerdy— we love learning, teaching, and keeping up to date with the latest research. We’re the most multidisciplinary and comprehensive team in private healthcare in BC; we put each client at the center of this with our goal to match everyone with the right clinician or team of clinicians. We take pride in our passionate clinicians, inspiring and uplifting facilities, high-quality health services, and exceptional customer service. We’re committed to delivering healthcare in the best possible way— and we have a singular culture of respect, warmth, curiosity and enthusiasm that makes being a part of the Tall Tree team something to be truly proud of.   
 Our occupational therapy team benefits from 1:1 mentorship, including report review and optional drop-in office hours, as well as a comprehensive onboarding program designed for both new graduates and clinicians new to private practice. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in weekly OT team meetings, where we unpack complex cases, share new interventions, and learn from guest speakers. Our monthly Lunch & Learns, curated by our in-house Director of Education and Learning, cover topics such as neuroplasticity and functional recovery, motivational interviewing in rehab, and advances in concussion management. Each year, we also gather for a staff retreat—part healthcare TED Talk, part lakeside recharge. Plus, through our sister company, AMP Healthcare, you’ll have access to discounted or free continuing education courses to keep your practice evolving. 
 Working collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team and providing services in our clinic, community settings, and through telehealth, you’ll craft personalized therapeutic plans that truly reflect the unique needs of each individual. 
 This is a unique opportunity for a dedicated professional who believes in doing healthcare the way it should be done—by focusing on genuine connections, effective solutions, and the overall health of the individuals we serve.
 Compensation: 
Full-time (5 days per week) community-based therapists have the opportunity to earn $118,000–$130,000+ annually , along with a signing bonus of up to $5,000 .

 As an Occupational Therapist at Tall Tree, you will:   
 Evaluate and assess patients using OT frameworks. You’ll develop individualized treatment plans, and provide exceptional care and interventions that are evidence-based, psychologically informed, and patient-centered.  
 Work collaboratively with our interdisciplinary team of Physiotherapists, Kinesiologists, Psychologists, Clinical Counselors, and more when indicated.  
 Collaborate with third party insurance funders , employers, and other relevant stakeholders. You’ll maintain related reports, records, and statistical data in accordance with established standards and procedures. 
 Keep growing. You’ll attend OT community of practice meetings and other educational opportunities available at Tall Tree. You’ll stay current with the latest evidence, findings, trends, and developments to ensure clients receive the best possible care.

 Someone qualified to practice Occupational Therapy in British Columbia. You are a member of the College of Occupational Therapists of British Columbia - with a preference for candidates with 2+ experience in private practice.  
 Clinical Excellence: You have a strong foundation in evidence-based practice and a commitment to mastering skills. You hold a profound respect for the complexity of human experience.  
 A commitment to growth: You have a deep passion for learning and continuous growth and development. You bring an openness to exploring new ideas and approaches to service delivery. 
 Great interpersonal and communication skills: You have a proven ability to collaborate effectively within a diverse team. You communicate clearly and effectively, whether you’re speaking, listening, or writing. You use precise language, compelling reassurance, healing narratives, and consistent messages. 
 Enthusiasm for teaching: You love sharing knowledge and can help mentor colleagues. 
 Humility and curiosity: You have an eagerness to learn and collaborate. 
 Strong Administrative Support:  Our incredible admin team handles reception, booking, billing, invoicing, and patient communication so you can focus on patient care. 
 Great Tools:  Access Jane for booking, charting, scheduling - anytime, anywhere. We also provide free access to Jane AI tools to make charting faster and easier. 
 Dedicated Marketing team:  Our in-house marketing team helps run advertising, promotion, and supports you to build your dream caseload. 
 Onboarding support like no other:  Structured onboarding plans to help you ramp up your caseload, connect with the team, and feel confident delivering the kind of patient-centered care we strive for.
 Mentorship & Collaboration:  Work alongside experienced clinicians and participate in mentorship, clinical workshops, and discipline-specific meetings where we share knowledge and discuss cases. 
 Ongoing Learning:  Join Lunch & Learns, journal clubs, and guest speaker sessions led by our Director of Education & Learning. You’ll also have access to discounted or complimentary courses through AMP Healthcare. 
 Professional Development:  Grow as a leader or educator through our Leadership Development Program and opportunities to lead workshops or share your expertise. 
 Performance-Based Recognition:  Our Senior Clinician Program recognizes clinical excellence and offers a pathway to increase your service pricing as your expertise grows. 
 Beautiful Clinics:  Work in thoughtfully designed clinics that create a welcoming space for patients and a great environment for clinicians. 
 Community & Connection:  Connect with colleagues through social events, learning sessions, and our annual Team Summit.

We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.


ABOUT THE CONSUMER BUSINESS SERVICES TEAM

 - Sierra partners with the businesses that power everyday life for consumers and enterprises alike — from the CPG brands on every shelf to the logistics networks that get products there, the real estate and facilities teams that manage the buildings people live and work in, and the energy and utility providers that keep the lights on. Our agents handle everything from order tracking and account management to field service scheduling and billing support, tuned to the voice and workflows of each business.

 - This vertical spans a wide range of industries — consumer products, commercial real estate, automotive & mobility, transportation & logistics, industrial manufacturing, information & data services, consumer electronics, professional services, facilities management, construction, energy, and utilities — giving you the breadth to build relationships across some of the largest and most established companies in the world.

 - Join us to bring AI agents to the businesses that quietly run the economy — and help build technology that makes these essential services faster, more reliable, and more human for everyone who depends on them.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Be the primary partner to your Sales counterparts helping to win deals and grow customers

 - Go from first discovery to a tailored, working agent in days, not weeks, across prospects and existing customers

 - Own the end-to-end technical pre-sales process by scoping customer use cases, articulating business value, designing and demoing Sierra’s incredible platform, leading technical and architecture reviews, and serving as the trusted technical expert throughout the sales cycle

 - Work directly with our Sales, Product and Agent Engineering teams to both drive our GTM function, as well as continuously improve our Agents through our customer-driven product development philosophy

 - Go deep on your industry, the patterns, and winning motions to scale your work


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 3-4+ years experience in Sales Engineering, Solutions Engineering or customer-facing technical sales

 - Experience in leading the sales process with Enterprise customers with deal sizes ranging $200-$500k

 - Past experience in demo building, and presenting, and working with customers or clients in the GTM function

 - Experience in relationship-building with prospects, including executives and technical leaders

 - A track record of handling a high number of deals concurrently without cutting quality, and comfortable switching between sub-industries and use cases

 - Bachelor's Degree or above; bonus if in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent professional experience


EVEN BETTER...

 - Selling a technical AI product


OUR VALUES

 - Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

 - Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

 - Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

About Fullscript
We’re an industry-leading health technology company on a mission to help people get better. We started in 2011 with one simple idea. Make it easier for practitioners to access the products they trust so they can deliver better care.
That simple idea grew into a platform that powers every part of care. Today, more than 125,000 practitioners use Fullscript for clinical insights, lab interpretations, patient analytics, education, and access to high-quality supplements. Over 10 million patients rely on Fullscript to stay connected to their care plans and follow through on treatment.
We build tools that make care smarter and more human. Tools that save time, simplify decisions, and help practitioners stay closely connected to the people they care for. When everything they need is in one place, they can focus on what matters most: helping people get better.
This is your invitation.
Bring your ideas, your grit, and your care for people.
Join us and shape the future of care.
The Opportunity
We’re looking for an Accounting Manager who understands accounting from end to end and knows how to turn that knowledge into better ways of working.
This role brings together accounting management and business transformation. You’ll lead our Accounts Payable team while rethinking the processes behind their work, identifying manual tasks, resolving bottlenecks, and implementing AI and automation that improve accuracy and help us scale.
Your primary focus will be Procure-to-Pay (P2P): how purchasing, inventory, vendor invoices, approvals, payments, and reconciliations connect to the general ledger and ultimately the P&L. You’ll bring the accounting judgment to understand what should be automated, what controls need to stay in place, and how changes affect financial reporting and audit requirements.
You’ll help define the path, working closely with Accounting, business teams, and systems partners to take improvements from initial opportunity through implementation, adoption, and measurable results.
What you'll do
Lead and develop the Accounts Payable team, setting clear priorities and supporting accurate, timely processing, payments, and reconciliations.
Map existing accounting and P2P workflows to identify repetitive tasks, manual handoffs, bottlenecks, and recurring errors.
Build and deliver an automation roadmap that moves targeted processes toward touchless processing, with clear controls and exception handling.
Own AI, automation, and process improvement projects from discovery and requirements through solution design, implementation, testing, training, and adoption.
Apply a full-cycle accounting perspective to process changes, ensuring transactions flow correctly into the GL and P&L and support accurate period-end reporting.
Improve the connections between purchasing, goods receiving, invoice matching, vendor management, approvals, payments, and reconciliations.
Partner with Accounting, Partner Managers, Distribution Centers, and systems teams to resolve root causes and redesign workflows across departments.
Strengthen approval controls, audit trails, reconciliations, and documentation as processes become more automated.
Evaluate and implement practical uses of AI and automation within accounting workflows, with appropriate validation and oversight.
Define and track measures such as touchless processing rates, exception volumes, processing time, accuracy, and manual effort saved.
Support audit readiness and financial reporting through reliable processes, complete documentation, and timely resolution of accounting issues.
What you bring to the table
Experience as an Accounting Manager, with a strong foundation in full-cycle accounting, the general ledger, reconciliations, period-end close, audit requirements, and the P&L.
A broad accounting background that allows you to assess how changes in AP and purchasing affect expense recognition, account balances, controls, and financial reporting.
Demonstrated experience implementing AI and automation in accounting or finance workflows. You’ve taken projects from identifying an opportunity through implementation, testing, adoption, and measuring results.
Experience delivering an accounting or finance system implementation, integration, or significant workflow redesign, with clear ownership of the outcome.
Practical knowledge of P2P processes, including vendor invoices, purchase orders, approvals, matching, payments, and reconciliations.
People management experience, including coaching, prioritizing work, and helping a team adopt new systems and processes.
Strong ERP knowledge and an understanding of how transactions move between operational systems and the GL.
The initiative to take a broad objective, investigate the problem, bring the right people together, and deliver improvements with minimal direction.
Clear communication skills and the ability to turn accounting requirements into practical solutions with business and technical partners.
Bonus if you have
A CPA designation and Big Four audit experience, both highly preferred.
Private industry accounting experience following public practice.
Experience in wholesale, distribution, manufacturing, retail, CPG, or another business where purchasing and physical inventory are central to operations.
Inventory accounting knowledge, including how purchasing, receiving, inventory balances, and related expenses flow through the financial statements.
Hands-on experience with NetSuite, SPS Commerce EDI, or similar ERP and transaction integration tools.
Practical experience applying tools such as ChatGPT or Claude to accounting work, supported by examples of how you validated outputs and improved a process.

RRSP match and competitive compensation packages to invest in your future

Great work happens when people feel supported, trusted, and inspired. At Fullscript, we stay curious and keep finding smarter ways to make care better. We grow together, take on new challenges, and focus on impact. We put people first, work as a team, and leave egos at the door.

Pelmorex operates at the intersection of weather, digital media, advertising, consumer technology, and B2B weather intelligence. Across the company, we generate and manage an unusually broad and valuable set of data: large-scale weather forecasts and observations, historical weather archives, consumer behavioural and location signals, digital product engagement, advertising yield, and commercial customer data.
We are seeking a Senior Manager, Data Strategy & Data Products to own and grow our enterprise and commercial data capabilities. This is a builder’s role at a pivotal inflection point. Third-party identifiers are receding, Canadian privacy legislation (Law 25, PIPEDA, Bill C-27) is evolving, and enterprise clients increasingly want to collaborate on privacy-safe data rather than buy off-the-shelf feeds.
This leader will serve as the business and product owner for Pelmorex’s data portfolio—connecting internal enterprise data foundations with our external commercial products across Audience Segments, Foot Traffic Attribution (FTA), and data collaboration environments (Clean Rooms).
Clear Ownership Division:
You will work in close partnership with technical leads and data engineering architectures. You own the "what, why, for whom, and priority," while technical lead counterparts own the "how." This is a strategy, commercial, and product leadership role focused on value realization, customer discovery, and product execution.
Please note, we are only considering candidates who are eligible to work in Canada and can work in a Hybrid model at our Oakville location.
 

WHAT'S THE DAY TO DAY LIKE?: 1. Data Product Strategy & Portfolio Ownership 
 Own the vision, commercial performance, roadmap, and delivery of Pelmorex's commercial and enterprise data product portfolio (Audience Segments, Foot Traffic Attribution, DSP data integrations, and Data Collaboration/Clean Rooms).
 Treat the data platform as a product, deeply understanding internal consumers (Consumer Product, Analytics, Sales) and external buyers (Agencies, Brands, Retail Media Networks).
 Track portfolio health, revenue targets, margins, and operational metrics, providing regular reporting and forecasting to executive leadership.
 Lead and mentor a team of Product Managers, setting direction, developing capability, and driving evidence-based decisions.
 2. Data Platform, Privacy & Collaboration Capabilities 
 Define and execute a privacy-safe data collaboration capability (Data Clean Rooms, secure enclaves) that enables clients and partners to combine datasets safely without exposing raw personal data.
 Partner with Legal and Privacy stakeholders to interpret and operationalize Quebec's Law 25, PIPEDA, and pending federal reforms into consent architecture, product requirements, and data retention rules.
 Set data source strategies, defining how weather, location, and behavioural signals are combined to create reusable enterprise data products (e.g., weather-triggered ad segments, yield models, and forecast verification metrics).
 Drive adoption of certified enterprise data products while migrating internal teams away from fragmented reporting and duplicate pipelines.
 3. Commercial & Client Partnerships 
 Work alongside Sales, Sales Operations, and B2B organizations to commercialize data products, join senior client calls, and shorten time-to-market.
 Package and price clean room and collaboration capabilities into standardized commercial product offerings rather than one-off custom solutions.
 Develop strategic data partnerships with agency holding companies, data providers, and adtech platforms.
 Act as a credible senior voice with clients on data strategy, matching architectures, and privacy-safe measurement.
 4. Cross-Functional Leadership 
 Partner closely with Engineering, Data Science, and Weather Science leadership to align roadmaps, sequence capacity, and resolve trade-offs.
 Translate business problems into clear requirements and measurable outcomes for technical development teams.
 Build business cases for data bets, demonstrating ROI through revenue growth, operational efficiency, speed, and competitive differentiation.

 Domain Expertise: Proven background in digital media, advertising, or data supply chains, with an understanding of DSPs, SSPs, audience taxonomies, and attribution methodologies.
 Data Collaboration & Privacy: Demonstrated experience with privacy-enhancing technologies or clean room platforms (e.g., InfoSum, LiveRamp, Habu, Snowflake, Databricks, or Google Ads Data Hub).
 Regulatory & Privacy Fluency: Practical understanding of Canadian privacy frameworks (Law 25, PIPEDA) as applied to commercial data products.
 Data Architecture Understanding: Strong working knowledge of modern data platforms, data pipelines, semantic layers, and identity resolution (understanding how data flows without needing to write code).
 Commercial Track Record: Demonstrated success owning commercial outcomes, pricing/packaging data capabilities, and driving measurable revenue or margin growth.
 Communication & Stakeholder Management: Exceptional ability to explain complex matching architecture to a CMO and business requirements to an engineer in the same day.
NICE TO HAVE: Experience launching a dedicated Data Clean Room or Data Collaboration product from scratch.
 Experience working with geospatial, location, or weather data assets.
 Bilingual in English and French.

Global Privacy Strategy & DPO

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence

The Lead AI Platform Engineer is accountable for technical leadership, engineering excellence, reliability, operability, and the controlled enablement of the organization’s enterprise AI platforms. 
This role provides hands-on technical leadership across AI platform design, implementation, automation, observability, and production readiness. The incumbent ensures AI platform services and solutions are secure, resilient, observable, supportable, and compliant with enterprise standards for reliability, security, platform management, monitoring, incident coordination, and governance control enforcement. 
The incumbent acts as a senior technical lead for platform engineering activities, guiding implementation decisions, establishing engineering patterns, mentoring team members, and partnering with cross-functional stakeholders to enable the safe and scalable adoption of AI across the enterprise.

: Main Activities: 
 AI Platform Engineering Leadership, Reliability and Operations 
 Lead the engineering, configuration, and operation of enterprise AI platforms to ensure availability, performance, resilience, and scalability across environments, integrations, and supporting infrastructure. 
 Define and implement platform engineering patterns, standards, reusable components, and operational guardrails that support secure and reliable AI solution delivery. 
 Provide technical leadership for platform triage, incident resolution, escalation coordination, and post-incident reviews to strengthen service stability and resilience. 
 Track and report on service reliability indicators, incident trends, engineering risks, and operational performance improvements. 
 AI Platform Enablement, Solution Readiness, Production Readiness and Technical Delivery 
 Lead technical enablement of approved AI use cases into non-production and production environments by ensuring environment readiness, dependency validation, release readiness, operational supportability, and service transition planning. 
 Partner with architecture, security, cloud, infrastructure, delivery, and application teams to translate solution requirements into secure, supportable, and scalable platform implementations. 
 Guide platform lifecycle management through release coordination, change readiness validation, maintenance planning, capacity planning, and technical risk mitigation. 
 Ensure AI platform changes meet defined engineering, operational, security, and control readiness criteria prior to release. 
 Observability, Automation and AI Ops Engineering 
 Design, implement, and continuously improve observability capabilities, including telemetry, logging, metrics, traces, dashboards, and alerting required for enterprise AI operations. 
 Lead automation initiatives using approved tools and practices to reduce manual effort, improve reliability, and standardize repeatable operational activities. 
 Analyze operational data to identify anomalies, recurring issues, root-cause patterns, performance bottlenecks, and opportunities for proactive service improvement. 
 Implement AI Ops use cases such as alert correlation, anomaly detection, forecasting, root-cause support, knowledge retrieval, and automation of repetitive operational tasks. 
 Mentor engineers on observability, automation, troubleshooting, and service reliability practices. 
 Governance, Risk and Control Engineering Execution 
 Embed governance, security, privacy, auditability, traceability, and human oversight requirements into AI platform engineering and operational practices. 
 Ensure platform implementations align with enterprise security policies, risk controls, compliance requirements, architecture standards, and operational readiness expectations. 
 Partner with security, risk, compliance, architecture, and data teams to assess implementation risks, close control gaps, and enable responsible deployment of AI capabilities. 
 Maintain documentation and evidence required for audit, governance reviews, production readiness checkpoints, and control validation. 
 Identify technical and control risks, recommend mitigation options, and escalate appropriately to relevant governance and risk stakeholders. 
 AI Asset Visibility, Platform Integrity, Operational Integrity and Engineering Standards 
 Maintain engineering and operational visibility of AI platform assets required for monitoring, support, ownership, lifecycle management, and cost alignment. 
 Validate asset ownership, relationships, configuration integrity, and lifecycle status in collaboration with application, platform, architecture, and infrastructure owners. 
 Establish and promote engineering standards, reusable patterns, documentation, and technical practices that improve platform supportability and operational integrity.
Knowledge/Skill Requirements:  : University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 
 7+ years of experience in platform engineering, site reliability engineering, DevOps, cloud operations, enterprise IT operations, or production platform support. 
 Demonstrated experience leading technical delivery, engineering standards, production readiness, incident response, problem management, service restoration, and operational reporting for enterprise platforms. 
 Technical Expertise: 
 Advanced experience with cloud platforms, observability, automation, configuration management, and integration patterns, including Azure Automation runbooks, Azure AI, Copilot integrations, AKS, virtual networks, App Service, and supporting Azure services. 
 Strong expertise with observability tools such as Azure Monitor, Application Insights, Log Analytics, Grafana, dashboards, alerting, and operational telemetry design. 
 Strong experience with CI/CD, automation, and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Logic Apps, Bicep, Terraform, Azure Policy, Key Vault, and related open-source technologies. 
 Knowledge of integration and event-driven technologies such as API Management, open-source API tools, Service Bus, Event Grid, and Apache Kafka.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to lead our Voice AI products. This is one of the fastest-growing line of business at Jobber and the clearest signal of where the company is headed next.

Jobber exists to serve small business owners—and our employer brand reflects that mission. Our customers are hard-working, hands-on entrepreneurs in industries like landscaping, HVAC, plumbing, and cleaning. They value reliability, speed, professionalism, and tools that help them work smarter and build stable lives for themselves and their families. Most are in the field, juggling priorities and relying on Jobber to keep their businesses moving. We care deeply about the real impact our product has on their day-to-day operations, their teams, and their communities.

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail's Canada's Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada's Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we've come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we've just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers.

The Product:

You’ll work across our rapidly-growing Communications products at Jobber. Receptionist, our headline Voice AI product, is the fastest-growing product at Jobber will be your primary focus. It’s the clearest expression of where we think this company goes next. In under two years it went from nothing to a multi-million dollar run-rate business, and today it answers thousands of calls a week for plumbers, cleaners, electricians, and landscapers who would otherwise have missed them. For a small home service business, a missed call isn't a missed notification. It’s missed revenue or a customer left in a lurch.

The Role:

You’ll lead the product strategy and execution for Jobber’s Voice products: products designed to help small service businesses to stay on top of their phone calls and keep their business moving even when they’re in a crawlspace or on a ladder.

We are looking for a product manager to take Receptionist from early, high-conviction customers to the majority of small businesses who could benefit from it.  Ultimately, you're building a business, not a feature. Jobber’s Voice product answers the phone and takes a message. Then it books the job, follows up on the quote, calls the customer back, and takes action inside Jobber on the service provider's behalf. Every new capability we ship is a new reason customers depend on us. You'll own the roadmap that takes us from receptionist to something much closer to an office manager.

The Product Manager will:

 - Turn Receptionist from a product early adopters love into one the majority of Jobber’s customers rely on daily.

 - Define and execute the roadmap for Receptionist and new Voice products balancing short-term wins with long-term innovation.

 - Deeply understand small business owners and office managers, synthesizing market, regulatory, and customer data into smart product decisions.

 - Prioritize user and business impact, ensuring every product decision drives value for Jobber’s small business customers.

 - Collaborate with domain experts across Voice AI, telephony and communications products to launch best-in-class products.

 - Act as the voice of the customer, especially for small business owners navigating an overflowing inbox.

 - Set the foundation for multi-product strategy, as we incorporate a full suite of communications and scale the business and team

To be successful, you should have:

 - Owned a revenue line — attach rate, pricing, or packaging — rather than engagement metrics alone.

 - Shipped (and improved) a production LLM or ML feature or product

 - Enough technical depth to be a real partner in architectural conversations about models, prompts, and pipelines.

 - Product management experience at a senior level, with evidence of shipping real things and seeing them through to long-term outcomes.

Highly desired (but not a deal-breaker) if you have:

 - A background in telephony or contact center technology — SIP, IVR, call routing, carrier and number registration.

 - Experience with consumer-facing conversational products

 - Familiarity with vertical SaaS, SMB, or home and field services.

 - Experience scaling products from 0 to 1 (and beyond)

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $145,900, a midpoint of $171,600, and a maximum salary of $197,400, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience, and against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us, too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

 At Hydro Ottawa, we empower the lives of the people in the communities we serve. 
 As the electricity distributor to the Nation’s Capital, our work powers the essential activities that make up our lives - at home, at work and at play. And as Ontario’s largest municipally-owned producer of green power, we are leading the way to a greener tomorrow. 
 We are seeking a Manager, Distribution Engineering & Asset Information, a change champion and innovative leader ready to embrace the opportunity to guide and mentor others, and enable them to do their best work. And in doing so, to leave a legacy.  
 Are you ready to make a difference in our community?
 JOB SUMMARY 
 Reporting to the Director, Distribution Engineering & Asset Management, the Manager, Distribution Engineering & Asset Information drives the near-to-mid-term engineering performance, customer connection execution, and foundational data integrity of Hydro Ottawa’s distribution system. Leading a multidisciplinary team, this role serves as the primary custodian of Hydro Ottawa’s Geographic Information System (GIS) data and its operational performance frameworks. By bridging advanced engineering analytics—such as Distributed Energy Resources (DER) integration, connection impact assessments, and power quality analytics—with robust GIS asset records and data governance, the Manager, Distribution Engineering & Asset Information ensures the grid remains resilient, compliant, and structurally optimized. Crucially, this role acts as an operational partner to the long-term planning team, translating day-to-day distribution system dynamics and asset data into the validated baseline models required to fuel Hydro Ottawa's strategic investment plans.
 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Lead, mentor, and manage a multidisciplinary team of supervisors, professional engineers, and technical specialists, establishing departmental goals, optimizing workload distribution, and conducting performance reviews to drive a high-performance operational and data-governance culture.
 Hold accountability for the integrity and maintenance of Hydro Ottawa's GIS data, governing record-management frameworks, GIS/CAD documentation standards, and network connectivity models to support safe grid management and corporate application interoperability.
 Spearhead the execution of Connection Impact Assessments, load assessments, and localized capacity evaluations to safely and efficiently integrate new customer loads and DERs 
 Guide technical staff through system performance analysis and root-cause investigations, ensuring findings are translated into actionable grid improvements.  
 Govern the engineering processes utilized for short-circuit calculations, protection coordination, and load flow models.
 Oversee validated engineering data, reliability risk assessments, and short-circuit models to support the long-term development, defense, and maintenance of the Distribution System Plan and Ontario Energy Board regulatory filings.
 Apply the corporate Value Framework and scoring methodologies to objectively prioritize localized, reliability-driven capital projects based on their capacity to enable immediate growth and mitigate system risks.
 Develop, defend, and strategically manage the department’s annual operational and maintenance budget, optimizing resource allocation across engineering analysis and technical GIS records workflows.
 Champion the Engineering Development Program within the department, actively guiding the mentorship, technical progression, and professional licensure of Engineer Interns to secure the engineering talent pipeline.
 Serve as the primary technical liaison and escalation point for external developers, electrical contractors, and cross-functional working groups to align customer interconnection timelines with Hydro Ottawa's capacity limits.
 Actively participate in the company's Business Continuity Plan, On-Call programs, and the Electricity Emergency Response Program.
 Formulate and deliver comprehensive technical presentations and engineering reports to departmental decision-makers, senior leadership, and diverse external stakeholders.
 Perform other duties as required.
 EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering from an accredited university 
 Professional Engineer licensed in the Province of Ontario
 Minimum of five (5) years of experience in a leadership role
 Experience in an electric utility engineering environment considered an asset
 Knowledge of ISO 55000 Asset Management considered an asset
 Strong computer skills; proficient in the use of office productivity and collaboration tools, preferably Google Workspace

 - You prefer inheriting a mature process over building it.

ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Getting paid is still one of the most manual parts of running a business. Finance teams chase invoices over email, match payments to invoices by hand in spreadsheets, and close the books late because cash data is scattered across banks, payment processors, and ERPs.

Ramp's Accounts Receivable team is building the system that automates all of it, from the moment an invoice is sent to the moment cash is reconciled in the general ledger. We own the full receivables lifecycle: invoicing, collections, payments, cash application, and accounting sync.

We're looking for a senior backend engineer to own core pieces of that system. The work sits where hard engineering problems meet real money: matching messy payment data to the right invoices, keeping ledgers correct to the cent, and syncing reliably with the accounting systems our customers depend on. You'll own projects end to end, from design through production, and work closely with product and design to turn complex finance workflows into software that just works.



WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build the payment-matching systems that automatically apply incoming ACH, wire, card, and check payments to the right invoices, even when payment details are incomplete or inconsistent

 - Design accurate data models where every dollar is traceable from invoice to payment to general ledger

 - Build two-way integrations with ERPs like NetSuite and QuickBooks that stay consistent through retries, partial failures, and edits on either side

 - Build collections workflows that help businesses get paid faster without hurting their customer relationships

 - Own projects from problem definition and technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

 - Raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship
   


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - Product sense: you care about the customer problem, not just the ticket, and you push back when the spec is wrong

 - Experience designing and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

 - Strong system design judgment and the ability to balance speed, correctness, reliability, and simplicity

 - A track record of independently owning complex projects and shipping high-quality software

 - Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach to technical decisions
   


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with invoicing, billing, payments, accounting, or other financial workflows

 - Experience building integrations that keep data consistent across systems

 - Experience improving reliability and operational visibility in a growing product

Do you want to make a difference in the lives of Canadians living with vision loss? 
 Vision Loss Rehabilitation Canada (VLRC) is a national health services organization dedicated to empowering people who are blind or partially sighted to live safely and independently. Our certified specialists provide client-centered rehabilitation, mobility training, and daily living skills programs that help clients build confidence and thrive. We work collaboratively with ophthalmologists, optometrists, and other health care professionals, offering essential care on a referral basis in homes, workplaces, and communities across the country. We value our employees as our greatest asset — and we’re committed to supporting their well-being, professional growth, and work-life balance. Learn more about VLRC at visionlossrehab.ca or call 1-844-887-8572.
 Position Title: Specialist, Low Vision
 Location: Toronto, ON
 Term: Full-time, Permanent (Existing vacancy)
 Reports To: Manager, Healthcare Operations
 Salary: $28.83/hour
 Posting Date: September 3, 2026
 Closing Date: September 18, 2026
 I. Scope and Summary of Primary Responsibilities 
 Performs Functional Low Vision Assessments, uses functional vision evaluation instruments to assess visual acuity, visual fields, contrast sensitivity function, color vision, stereopsis, visual perceptual and visual motor functioning, literacy skills in reading and writing, etc. as they relate to vision impairment and disability. The Specialist also evaluates work history, educational performance, use of technology, quality of life and aspects of psychosocial and cognitive function. They also instruct in the use of prescribed low vision devices.
 II. Essential Functions 
 This position entails, but is not limited to the following general responsibilities: 
 ·        Conducts functional low vision assessments.
 ·        Teaches individuals with partial sight how to maximize residual vision.  
 ·        Recommends and trains in the use of optical and non-optical aids.
 ·        Educates individuals about their eye condition and vision health.
 ·        Refers individuals to other internal and external services.  
 ·        Handles public inquiries regarding vision health and low vision services.
 ·        Conducts research on new optical aids, adaptive equipment, and new findings in the eye care field.  
 ·        Attends professional development training and conferences as required. 
 ·        Delivers public speaking seminars and workshops on low vision services and related topics to community agencies/groups and health care professionals. 
 ·        Interprets medical information.
 ·        Performs administrative duties, including, but not limited to, data input, documentation of assessments/client contact, and applicable subsidy program(s) as appropriate.
 Relationships 
 ·        Liaises and builds relationships with community-based   rehabilitation teams, agencies, schools, partners, health practitioners and stakeholders.
 ·        Provides support and consultation to individuals and their families regarding adjustment to vision loss.
 ·        Attends and participates in multi-disciplinary team meetings. 
 ·        Promotes an understanding and awareness of vision health related issues through consultation, public education, and in-service training.
 ·        Assists with the training, placement and supervision of volunteers and students. 
 Problem Solving 
 ·        Provide timely delivery of low vision services to ensure individuals with vision loss acquire travel skills to remain/regain independence.
 ·        Ability to creatively and quickly problem solve to respond to unique individual needs. 
 Decision Autonomy 
 ·        Utilizes standard procedures and processes to work with individuals on developing an individual program to accommodate their unique needs.
 ·        Utilizes judgment when determining if the individual requires referral to another VLRC service or external services. 
 Leadership 
 ·        Takes initiative to keep abreast of new electronic travel aids and other advances/technologies and techniques in Orientation and mobility.
 ·        Takes initiative to be knowledgeable of guide dog schools and their programs.
 ·        Provides leadership to community groups and partners by educating, advocating and promoting awareness about vision loss.
 ·        Provides mentorship supervision to apprentice staff within the organization, leadership in training and coaching volunteers, students and staff.
 ·        Facilitate and enhance team efforts on a professional level and share specialized knowledge, sources, experience, concepts, and skills. 
 III. Qualifications 
 Knowledge and Skill Requirements 
 ·        Demonstrated knowledge of ocular anatomy, physiology, pathology, and low vision rehabilitation including optical and non-optical aids, visual skills and adaptive technology, blindness, and deaf-blindness and the psychosocial aspects of vision loss.
 ·        Demonstrated ability to facilitate group education.
 ·        Knowledgeable about disabilities and all life stages (children to seniors) 
 ·        Demonstrated decision making and professional judgement.
 ·        Mature and professional attitude
 ·        Self-directed, organized, and excellent attention to detail.
 ·        Demonstrated individual centred approach and commitment.
 Experience and Education 
 ·        All personnel hired to provide low vision services must meet the requirements of the VLRC National Vision Rehabilitation (Low Vision Specialist) Training Program. 
 ·        Must be graduates from a post secondary institution with a major in health care or vision i.e. public health or community nursing.  ACVREP Certified Low Vision Therapists, COC, AOC, or equivalent Certified Orthoptists, and JCAHPO certified allied health personnel in ophthalmology.
 ·        Eligible for ACVREP certification.
 ·        Undergraduate degree or equivalent.
 ·        High level of competency in relevant computer applications.
 ·        Excellent verbal, written and math skills.
 ·        French is considered an asset.
 Work Environment 
 ·        Service will be provided in office centers, individual homes and/or the community.
 ·        Willingness to work flexible hours.
 ·        Travel will be required.
 At VLRC, your work has real impact. Join a team that empowers Canadians with vision loss to live independently, and where your growth, well-being, and contributions matter. We offer:
 ·        Comprehensive benefits for health, vision, dental, corporate discounts employee and family assistance program
 ·        Flexible work arrangements, generous paid time off, and work-life balance initiatives
 ·        Career development through training, mentorship, and advancement opportunities
 ·        Inclusive work culture with supportive teams, employee recognition, joy in work wellness program, and mental health supports
  Join us to grow your career and make a difference everyday.
 Inclusion, Accessibility & Accommodation 
 VLRC is committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive, equitable, and accessible workplace. We welcome applications from members of groups that have been historically marginalized, including but not limited to Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, including those who are blind, partially sighted, or deafblind, women and 2SLGBTQ+. We strongly encourage applications from applicants with sight loss to apply.  Le rôle de Product Owner / Analyste d’affaires est essentiel pour traduire les besoins des parties prenantes en exigences claires et réalisables. À la croisée des affaires et des technologies, la personne titulaire du poste contribue à définir la vision du produit, à prioriser les besoins et à assurer la livraison de solutions qui répondent aux objectifs de l’organisation.
 Elle agit comme intermédiaire entre les parties prenantes, les équipes de développement et les utilisateurs finaux, tout en favorisant la collaboration et l’amélioration continue dans un environnement de travail agile
 À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien? 
 Vision & Stratégie du Produit : 
 Agir en tant que principal point de contact entre les parties prenantes (entreprise, clients et équipes de développement).
 Recueillir les avis, les retours et les exigences des propriétaires d'entreprise, des clients et des autres parties prenantes pour s'assurer que le produit répond à leurs besoins.
 Organiser des sessions régulières de retour d'information et de révisions avec les parties prenantes pour garantir l'alignement.
 Développer et maintenir une feuille de route décrivant les fonctionnalités du produit, les améliorations et les livrables.

 Créer des documents de requis d’affaires et fonctionnels détaillés.
 Créer, maintenir et prioriser le backlog produit, en veillant à ce qu'il soit clair et réalisable pour l'équipe de développement.
 Rédiger des histoires utilisateurs détaillées, définir les critères d'acceptation et garantir la clarté des exigences.
 Prioriser en continu les tâches en fonction de la valeur commerciale, de la demande du marché et de la faisabilité technique.
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de développement, y compris les ingénieurs logiciels, les concepteurs et les testeurs, pour garantir une compréhension partagée des exigences et des priorités.

 Collaborer avec les parties prenantes pour définir les critères d'acceptation. Veiller à ce que les fonctionnalités livrées respectent les normes de qualité et les attentes des utilisateurs.
 Effectuer des tests d'acceptation utilisateur (UAT) pour valider que les solutions livrées répondent aux exigences commerciales et aux besoins des utilisateurs.

About the Role 
 We are seeking an experienced and safety-focused Mobile Crane Operator to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for safely operating a diverse fleet of mobile cranes. Working closely with supervisors, site personnel, and project teams, you will execute lifting operations safely, efficiently, and in accordance with all regulatory requirements and company standards.
 Our fleet includes 20+ tonne boom cranes, an 80 tonne Terex AT crane, and a Grove 350 tonne crane with lifting capacities ranging from approximately 20 tonnes to 350 tonnes . 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Crane Operations 
 Safely operate a variety of mobile cranes to complete lifting activities 
 Set up, inspect, and dismantle cranes in accordance with manufacturer specifications and site requirements. 
 Review lift plans, load charts, rigging configurations, and site conditions prior to each lift. 
 Perform safe lifting, positioning, loading, unloading, and placement of equipment and materials. 
 Monitor weather conditions, ground stability, and other environmental factors that may impact lifting operations. 
 Adapt lifting plans as site conditions change while maintaining a strong focus on safety. 
 Equipment Maintenance & Compliance 
 Complete daily pre-operational inspections and document equipment condition. 
 Perform routine maintenance, cleaning, and minor troubleshooting of assigned equipment. 
 Maintain accurate daily operating logs, inspection reports, and maintenance records. 
 Immediately report equipment deficiencies, hazards, or incidents. 
 Teamwork & Safety 
 Work collaboratively with supervisors, site personnel, and other team members to coordinate safe and efficient lifting operations. 
 Communicate effectively throughout all lifting activities to ensure work is completed safely and efficiently. 
 Follow all Occupational Health & Safety legislation, company policies, and industry best practices. 
 Promote a strong safety culture by identifying hazards and participating in ongoing safety initiatives
 Minimum 5 years of experience operating mobile cranes. 
 Valid 339A Mobile Crane Operator Certificate of Qualification (Red Seal) . 
 Valid DZ driver's licence required; AZ licence is considered an asset. 
 Thorough understanding of crane load charts, lift planning, rigging practices, and safe lifting procedures. 
 Strong mechanical aptitude with the ability to perform basic equipment inspections and routine maintenance. 
 Excellent communication and teamwork skills. 
 Ability to work independently while adapting to changing priorities and changing job site conditions. 
 Commitment to maintaining the highest standards of safety and professionalism. 
 Driver's License and own vehicle required
